data.narrative:
Stegra, a Growth-stage climate and energy company founded by Carl-Erik Lagercrantz and Harald Mix, has raised $7.0B+ to date. The valuation landscape for frontier-tech companies in this sector includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers spanning similar technology verticals, though no direct same-stage peer set exists with sufficient depth for reliable median multiples.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($7.0B) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement yields $8.4B. A peer-median approach was not viable; while eight Climate & Energy peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier produced insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to support a robust public or private comparable baseline.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $7.1B to $9.7B, centered on $8.4B. Material uncertainties include the absence of narrow-band peer multiples, which limits confidence in stage-progression step-up assumptions, and the methodological constraint of relying on a single triangulation pillar. Additional comparable transactions or disclosed Growth-stage financing rounds in climate tech would materially narrow this range. The upper and lower bounds reflect ±15% sensitivity around the central estimate.
